Linear elliptic problems

Source: R/elliptic.R
elliptic_problem.Rd

elliptic_problem() defines the scalar second-order problem

Usage

elliptic_problem(
  mesh,
  diffusion = 1,
  reaction = 0,
  advection = NULL,
  source = 0,
  bcs = list(),
  degree = 1,
  stabilization = c("none", "supg"),
  quad_degree = NULL
)

poisson_problem(
  mesh,
  diffusion = 1,
  source = 0,
  boundary = list(),
  degree = 1,
  bcs = boundary
)

Arguments

mesh

A pde_mesh().

diffusion

Diffusion coefficient k.

reaction

Reaction coefficient c (non-negative for coercivity).

advection

Velocity b, or NULL.

source

Source f.

bcs

A pde_bc or list of them. Boundary edges without a condition receive the natural condition k du/dn = 0.

degree

Lagrange degree (1 or 2).

stabilization

"none" or "supg".

quad_degree

Quadrature exactness degree (default 2 degree + 2).

boundary

Alias of bcs for poisson_problem().

Value

An object of class pde_problem (subclass elliptic_problem).

Details

-div(k grad u) + b . grad u + c u = f in the domain,

with Dirichlet, Neumann and Robin boundary conditions. poisson_problem() is the special case b = 0, c = 0.

The weak form is: find u with the Dirichlet data such that for all test functions v vanishing on the Dirichlet boundary

int k grad u . grad v + (b . grad u) v + c u v + sum_Robin int alpha u v = int f v + sum_Neumann int g v + sum_Robin int r v.

Coefficients may be numbers or vectorized function(x, y); diffusion may also be a constant symmetric positive definite 2 by 2 matrix, and advection a length-2 vector or a function returning a two-column matrix. Uniform ellipticity (k > 0) is checked at the quadrature points.

With stabilization = "supg" (P1 only) the streamline upwind Petrov-Galerkin terms sum_T tau_T int_T (b . grad u + c u - f) (b . grad v) are added, with tau_T = h_T / (2 |b|) (coth(Pe) - 1 / Pe), Pe = |b| h_T / (2 k), evaluated at the element centroid with h_T the longest edge (for a matrix K, k is the streamline diffusivity b'Kb / |b|^2). For P1 elements the diffusive part of the element residual vanishes, so the method is consistent when the diffusion is constant; with variable diffusion the term grad k . grad u_h is omitted, which keeps the convergence order but is not strictly consistent.

A connected part of the domain (mesh components joined by periodic conditions) on which no Dirichlet value, reaction term or Robin term with positive alpha acts keeps the constants in its kernel: there the solution is unique only up to a constant. The solver gauges each such component separately, checks its compatibility condition (for a symmetric operator int f + int g = 0 over the component) and returns the solution with zero mean on it, labeled as such. Components that are anchored are solved as usual. The compatibility defect is read from the Lagrange multiplier of the zero-mean constraint, after the load is normalized, and compared with compatibility_tol * sum_i |b_i| over the component (an argument of solve_pde(), default 1e-6, at most 0.01). For a nonsymmetric operator (advection) the left null vector is not constant, and data that are compatible for the PDE leave a discrete defect of the size of the discretization error. A relative defect up to (h / diameter)^2 is then accepted silently, one up to one percent with a warning, and anything larger is an error on every mesh: the discrete equations have no solution, and refining the mesh is the remedy when the data are compatible. Whenever the defect is above rounding level (1e-10), the returned function solves the equations with the source shifted by the multiplier times the constant mass, not the original ones: diagnostics$gauge$modified is then TRUE, diagnostics$gauge$original_problem_solved is FALSE, and diagnostics$solver$relative_residual is the residual of the original equations.

References

Brooks, A. N. and Hughes, T. J. R. (1982). Streamline upwind/Petrov-Galerkin formulations for convection dominated flows. Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering, 32, 199-259.

Examples

mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8)
prob <- poisson_problem(mesh, source = function(x, y) 2 * pi^2 * sin(pi * x) * sin(pi * y),
                        boundary = dirichlet_bc(0))
sol <- solve_pde(prob)
sol
#> <pde_solution> P1, 81 dofs; solver cholesky (solved), relative residual 1.54e-15
#>   u range [    0, 0.9872]
